_about: ASSEMBLIES goal WP0.2 input: which engineering firm drafted each locally present corpus document, so the dev / held-out split can keep one drafter's documents on one side. Evidence is the PDF's own text layer (title blocks) or sets.json provenance, gathered 2026-09-23 with pymupdf page.get_text(); a firm is named only where that text names it. A document with no identifiable firm is its own group. Two documents are grouped when the text shows a shared firm or a shared design team; that is deliberately conservative (it can only make the held-out side harder, never leak a drafter into it). Byte-identical documents are marked duplicate_of and never counted twice. Firms were re-checked against a render of each document's title block on 2026-09-23 (before the split was drawn); two text-layer attributions were corrected that way (federal-mech, 031/040).

_about_second_tier: Extended 2026-09-26 (AS-17) to every eligible unseen corpus document: the firm comes from the cover sheet's design-team listing and the title block's text, and every document's title block was also checked by eye on a low-resolution render of one sheet (46 dpi strips, which can clip schedule fragments; every eligible document was viewed alike, before the second tier was drawn). A firm printed only as an image has no text form (015_VA's 'MN+BMcD Joint Venture', 038_NC's Coffman Engineers logo); those two were found this way and join their held-out drafter's group. The grouping rule is unchanged: a shared design firm of record (architect, engineer or consultant) groups documents; a shared owner, owner's template or owner's reviewers does not, with one conservative exception: USDA ARS in-house designs are grouped as one design organization with held-out 018_GA.
